questions.question: SARS-CoV-2 and MERS-CoV question.

parts.text: Name three key features that allowed SARS-CoV-2 to become the source of the current pandemic (as opposed to MERS-CoV), not related to social factors or pandemic management.

parts_raw.text: Name 3 key features that allowed SARS-COV2 to become the source of the current pandemic (vs. MERS not) (not related to social factors or pandemic management)

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Receptor use and tropism: SARS-CoV-2 spike binds ACE2, which is abundantly expressed on upper respiratory epithelium, giving efficient nasopharyngeal replication and respiratory droplet/aerosol spread; MERS-CoV uses DPP4, expressed mainly in the lower respiratory tract, so shedding from the upper airway is poor. (2) Efficient sustained human-to-human transmission (R0 approximately 2-3 with a polybasic furin cleavage site in spike enhancing entry into airway cells), whereas MERS-CoV transmission is largely zoonotic from dromedary camels with only limited, mostly nosocomial, human chains (R0 <1). (3) High rate of pre-symptomatic and asymptomatic/mildly symptomatic infection with peak viral shedding at or just before symptom onset, allowing undetected transmission; MERS-CoV causes severe disease with high case-fatality (about 35%) late in illness, so cases are identified and isolated.

questions.question: MERS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2 are both coronaviruses.

parts.text: What are three reasons, not social or related to pandemic management, why SARS-CoV-2 is so different, i.e. why it caused a pandemic?

parts_raw.text: MERS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2 are both coronaviruses. What are 3 reasons that aren’t social or pandemic management for why SARS-CoV-2 is so different, i.e why it caused a pandemic?

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Receptor: SARS-CoV-2 spike uses ACE2, highly expressed in the upper airway, giving high nasopharyngeal viral loads and easy droplet/aerosol spread; MERS-CoV uses DPP4, concentrated in the lower respiratory tract. (2) Intrinsic transmissibility: efficient sustained human-to-human spread (R0 approximately 2-3), aided by the polybasic furin cleavage site at the S1/S2 junction; MERS-CoV requires repeated camel-to-human introductions and has R0 <1. (3) Pre-symptomatic/asymptomatic shedding with peak viral load around symptom onset and a comparatively low case-fatality rate, so infected people transmit while well; MERS causes severe, readily recognized illness (CFR about 35%) with transmission late in disease.

parts.text: Besides the S protein, list the other three structural proteins.
What is the mechanism of action of remdesivir?
Name two viruses that remdesivir may be effective in treating as shown in animal models.

parts_raw.text: Besides the S protein, list the other 3 structural proteins
What is the mechanism of action for Remdesivir
Name two viruses that Remdesivir may be effective in treating as shown in animal models

questions.model_answer:
a) (1) Membrane (M). (2) Envelope (E). (3) Nucleocapsid (N).
b) Remdesivir is a monophosphoramidate prodrug of an adenosine nucleoside analogue; it is metabolized intracellularly to the active triphosphate, which competes with ATP for incorporation by the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (nsp12) and causes delayed chain termination, stalling viral RNA synthesis. It also evades proofreading by the coronavirus nsp14 exonuclease.
c) (1) MERS-CoV (and SARS-CoV) in mouse and rhesus macaque models. (2) Ebola virus (also Marburg and Nipah viruses in nonhuman primate models).

cohort_answer.text: Proteins: E protein (envelope); M protein (membrane); N protein (nucleocapsid). Remdesivir MOA: It is a prodrug, nucleoside analog, inhibits viral replication by inhibiting RNA dependent RNA polymerase enzyme, inserting itself into RNA product and stalling RNA synthesis. Other viruses: Other coronaviruses (Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus), Ebola, Marburg (Filoviruses)

questions.question: COVID-19 (viruses).

parts.text: Name three proteins aside from the spike protein.
Name one approved treatment for mpox.
Describe remdesivir treatment efficacy as per animal models.

parts_raw.text: 3 proteins aside from Spike protein
1 approved treatment for Mpox
Remdesivir treatment efficacy as per animal models

questions.model_answer:
a) (1) Envelope (E). (2) Membrane (M). (3) Nucleocapsid (N).
b) Tecovirimat (TPOXX), an inhibitor of the orthopoxvirus VP37 envelope-wrapping protein required for formation and dissemination of infectious virions. (Brincidofovir/cidofovir are alternatives.)
c) In rhesus macaques inoculated with SARS-CoV-2 and treated with remdesivir 12 hours after inoculation, treated animals had no or markedly reduced respiratory disease (only 1 of 6 with dyspnea vs all untreated controls), lower lung viral loads and less severe lung pathology, though no reduction in upper respiratory shedding. Similar prophylactic and early-therapeutic benefit was shown in MERS-CoV macaque and mouse models and in Ebola virus-infected macaques.

cohort_answer.text:
3 proteins: Envelope; Membrane; Nucleocapsid.
Approved treatment for Mpox: Tecovirimat (Tpoxx) - potent inhibitor of an orthopoxvirus protein required for formation of an infectious virus particle, essential for dissemination within an infected host. (Cidofovir has in vitro activity against monkeypox virus and shown effective against lethal monkeypox virus challenge in animal models.)
Remdesivir efficacy in animal models: In a study of 12 macaques, 6 treated with Remdesivir and 6 not; of the 6 treated only 1 developed dyspnea vs all of the untreated. Outpatient treatment: 4/246 (1.6%) treated arm vs 21/252 (8.3%) placebo arm required a medical visit. Inpatient treatment: 1062 randomized to remdesivir or placebo; median recovery time 10 days vs 15 days; mortality at day 15: 6.7% vs 11.9%; mortality at day 29: 11.4% vs 15.2%.
